pull.title: rpc: reject AssumeUTXO rollback without tip data
pull.body:
**Problem:** Loading a UTXO snapshot on a pruned node can leave the active tip without block or undo data. Attempting a rollback with `dumptxoutset` then triggers an assertion and terminates the node.

**Fix:** Reuse `GetPruneHeight` to reject rollback with the existing pruning error when the required data is unavailable.

events.body: The following sections might be updated with supplementary metadata relevant to reviewers and maintainers. ### External sites * Code coverage & benchmarks: https://corecheck.dev/bitcoin/bitcoin/pulls/36503 * Ralph review https://git.fish.foo/bitcoin/bitcoin/pulls/36503#author-ralph ### Reviews See [the guideline](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#code-review) and [AI policy](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/master/doc/AI_POLICY.md) for information on the review process. | Type | Reviewers | | ---- | --------- | | Concept ACK | [musaHaruna](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36503#pullrequestreview-5492606225), [danielabrozzoni](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36503#pullrequestreview-6039733757) | | Stale ACK | [cyb3ralbert](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36503#pullrequestreview-5870781677) | If your review is incorrectly listed, please copy-paste <!--meta-tag:bot-skip--> into the comment that the bot should ignore. ### Conflicts Reviewers, this pull request conflicts with the following ones: * [#36778](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36778) (AssumeUTXO: replace `loadtxoutset` RPC with a startup arg by l0rinc) * [#36702](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36702) (validation: don't treat snapshot block as linked on startup by shuv-amp) * [#36266](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36266) (rpc: Let dumptxoutset fail early on stale targets and concurrent runs by fjahr) If you consider this pull request important, please also help to review the conflicting pull requests. Ideally, start with the one that should be merged first.

Concept ACK. The fix looks straightforward and contained: `GetPruneHeight` handles missing data at the tip before calling `GetFirstBlock`, allowing the RPC to return an error instead of hitting the assertion.

I have a few questions about the surrounding behavior. 

- Should the early availability check also cover non-pruned nodes? They can load a snapshot without having the historical block or undo data. I understand that the code limits the early check to pruning mode, and non-pruned nodes can fail later during rollback. Could checking availability earlier avoid copying the UTXO set before discovering that rollback is impossible? Registering `TemporaryPruneLock` could still remain conditional on `IsPruneMode()`.

- Would a more general error message describe these cases better? Specifically, changing:
`Could not roll back to requested height since necessary block data is already pruned.`
to:
`Could not roll back to requested height because required block or undo data is unavailable.`
After loading a UTXO snapshot, the node may lack historical block or undo data because it has not obtained or generated it yet, not because pruning deleted it. Keeping the existing wording for this focused fix seems reasonable, though.

- Could the boundary eventually compare the highest missing-data height against the target using `>` instead of `>=`? The loop in `CreateRolledBackUTXOSnapshot` uses: `while (block_index->nHeight > target->nHeight)`
For example, exporting state 299 from tip 301 disconnects blocks 301 and 300, so it does not need undo for block 299. If `GetPruneHeight` returns 299, the current `299 >= 299` check rejects that request, whereas `299 > 299` would allow it. Am I missing another requirement for the target’s data?
In a locally modified version using `>` and applying the early availability check to both pruned and non-pruned nodes, the added boundary tests passed. Exporting state 299 succeeded and matched the original snapshot’s UTXO hash, while exporting state 298 still failed.

rpc: check block and undo data above rollback target

Rollback disconnects only blocks above the requested height. Check those blocks for missing body or undo data before copying the UTXO set on pruned nodes and snapshot chainstates.
Report unavailable data because snapshot history may not yet have been downloaded.

Suggested in https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36503#pullrequestreview-5492606225

-        assert_raises_rpc_error(-1, "Could not roll back to requested height since necessary block data is already pruned.",

+        check_rollback_unavailable(n1)

comments.body: I think this is fine to leave, it proves that n1 has the block data for snapshot_block, it's only missing undo data

Came up during review with Opus 5:

In master we currently allow to call `dumptxoutset` with `rollback=0`, and the call will succeed as long as we are non pruned, and will produce an empty snapshot.

With this PR, we introduce another case where `rollback=0` is allowed, although much more exotic: pruned nodes but with all the block+undo data available, which can happen if one sets `prune=1` and then doesn't prune anything, or if a pruned node is in early IBD.
(In master this doesn't work, because `GetFirstBlock` excludes the genesis block as it has no undo data, and the rollback would fail with "Could not roll back to requested height since necessary block data is already pruned.", despite not having anything pruned. In this sense, this PR removes a confusing error that the user could get)

In both cases, the snapshot produced is not wrong, it's simply expensive to create and useless. Not sure if it's worth to fix, but wanted to mention :)

See: https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/compare/master...danielabrozzoni:bitcoin:assumeutxo_rollback_0 - I pushed one commit to show the current behavior, the tree commits from this PR, and one test change to show the new behavior.
